25.explanation: The Supreme Court (Number of Judges) Amendment Act, 2019 raised the sanctioned strength from 30 to 33 judges, excluding the CJI.

sources.title: Supreme Court (Number of Judges) Amendment Act, 2019

26.explanation: Under Art. 124(1) Parliament fixes the number of judges by ordinary law (Supreme Court (Number of Judges) Act, 1956), so a simple majority is enough.

27.explanation: Under Art. 124(2) the President appoints Supreme Court judges, in practice on the collegium's recommendation.

28.explanation: Supreme Court judges retire at 65 (Art. 124(2)). High Court judges retire at 62.

29.explanation: Art. 131 is original jurisdiction, Art. 136 is special leave to appeal, and Art. 143 is advisory jurisdiction.

30.explanation: Under Art. 124(4) the President removes a judge after an address by each House passed by a special majority (majority of total membership and two-thirds of those present and voting).

31.explanation: When Modi and Carney met at the Évian G7 on 16 June 2026, they reaffirmed the aim of concluding CEPA negotiations in 2026.

32.explanation: The G7 has about 10% of the world's population but roughly 43–45% of global nominal GDP.

33.explanation: The G7 is an informal forum with no founding treaty, permanent secretariat or headquarters. The presidency rotates every year.

34.explanation: The presidency rotation runs Canada (2025), France (2026, Évian), then the United States (2027).

35.explanation: Education has been in the Concurrent List (Entry 25, List III) since the 42nd Amendment (1976) moved it from the State List.

sources.title: Constitution of India, Seventh Schedule, List III Entry 25

36.explanation: ULLAS stands for Understanding of Lifelong Learning for All in Society, the name of the New India Literacy Programme.

37.explanation: ULLAS (2022–27) is a Centrally Sponsored Scheme implemented jointly by the Centre and the States/UTs.

38.explanation: The Department of School Education and Literacy, Ministry of Education administers ULLAS.

39.explanation: Learners and volunteers register and track progress on the ULLAS mobile app and portal, with content on DIKSHA.

40.explanation: ULLAS gives adults aged 15+ who missed school foundational literacy, numeracy and critical life skills.

41.explanation: Ahmedabad, India was confirmed as host of the 2030 (centenary) Commonwealth Games.

42.explanation: Glasgow 2026's 10 sports were athletics, swimming, artistic gymnastics, track cycling, netball, weightlifting, boxing, judo, bowls and 3x3 basketball. Hockey was dropped.

43.explanation: Shooting and wrestling have historically brought India its largest Commonwealth Games medal hauls.

sources.title: Wikipedia: India at the Commonwealth Games

44.explanation: The first Games, the 1930 British Empire Games, were held in Hamilton, Canada.

45.explanation: India finished 4th at Glasgow 2026 with 39 medals (13 gold, 17 silver, 9 bronze), behind Australia, England and Canada.

sources.title: Free Press Journal: India jump to 4th, total 39

46.explanation: Gulveer Singh won silver in the 10,000 m and bronze in the 5,000 m at Glasgow 2026, the only Indian with two medals at those Games. The question's wording 'first ever' overstates it; read it as within Indian athletics.

sources.title: The Bridge: Seven boxing golds, Gulveer Singh history

46.note: Question wording 'FIRST to win TWO medals at a single CWG edition' is historically imprecise (Indian shooters have won multiple medals at one Games); intended answer is unambiguous.

47.explanation: Baba Gurdit Singh chartered the Komagata Maru (1914) to challenge Canada's 'continuous journey' regulation, which in practice barred Indian immigrants.

48.explanation: Almost all of the 376 passengers were from Punjab, mostly Sikhs.

50.explanation: The Komagata Maru sailed from Hong Kong (via Shanghai and Yokohama) to Vancouver. On its return, passengers were fired on at Budge Budge.
